official.deadline_note: Cohort 4 (Phase II) applications ran 20 August to 10 September 2026 and have now closed. Phase II is expected to support at least 280 students across three cohorts from 2025, so a further cohort is expected on the same annual cycle, but no next-cohort window is published as of 2026-10-10.
official.application_cycle: Phase II, Cohort 4 (KfW-funded); call published 13 August 2026
official.status_note: The published Cohort 4 call closed on 10 September 2026 at 17:00 East Africa Time. As of 2026-10-10 the IUCEA 'Call for applications' page lists no newer EACSP cohort; Phase II covers three cohorts, so further calls are expected but not yet dated.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full tuition fees payable directly to the host university.
benefits: One return economy-class air ticket between the scholar's home country and the host country upon commencement and completion of studies
Full tuition fees payable directly to the host university
Arrival allowance of EUR 200 upon arrival in the study country and opening a bank account there
A monthly stipend of EUR 380 to cover accommodation, meals, local transport and other living expenses
A lump-sum allowance of EUR 650 for study materials
A one-time EUR 1,500 study and research allowance
Medical insurance coverage for the duration of the scholarship
Visa/entry fee where payment of an entry pass into the host country or student pass is required
Participation in at least one extracurricular event
eligibility: Be a citizen of any of the 8 EAC Partner States: Burundi, Democratic Republic of Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania and Uganda
Be below 35 years of age at the time of application
Apply to study in an EAC Partner State other than the country of citizenship
Possess a Bachelor's degree with a minimum of Second Class Upper Division, Distinction or equivalent qualification
Have applied for admission to an eligible Master's programme offered by a partner university
Submit a complete scholarship application within the stipulated application period
requirements: Applications must be submitted in English and in accordance with the application guidelines
Complete both stages of the process: apply for admission to an eligible Master's programme at a participating university, and submit a separate EAC Scholarship Programme application
Submit all mandatory supporting documents; failure to do so results in the application being deemed incomplete and ineligible
Applicants applying for more than one programme must submit a separate complete application - a separately completed online form and a separate email with a complete document set - for each programme

Academic qualifications obtained outside the host country must be equated by the relevant National Council/Commission for Higher Education or other competent authority in the host country before admission
documents: E02 Recent colour passport photograph of full head and upper shoulders (mandatory)
E03 Proof of university admission application - admission letter, acknowledgement email, receipt or portal screenshot (mandatory)
E04 Certified true copies of the Bachelor's degree certificate and academic transcript (mandatory)
E06 Bank statements for the last six months, where applicable (mandatory)
E24 English language proficiency certificate such as IELTS or TOEFL, where applicable (optional supporting document; no minimum score published)
selection_criteria: Only complete applications for eligible programmes, submitted before the deadline, in English and in accordance with the application guidelines, are considered
Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted
Providing false, misleading or incomplete information may result in automatic disqualification or withdrawal of a scholarship award; IUCEA reserves the right to verify all submitted information

Female applicants, persons with disabilities and applicants from other disadvantaged backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply; the Programme aims for at least 50% female participation among beneficiaries
coverage: Full tuition fees paid directly to the host university
Monthly EUR 380 stipend covering accommodation, meals, local transport and other living expenses
Return economy-class air ticket between home and host country
EUR 200 arrival allowance and EUR 650 lump-sum study-materials allowance
One-time EUR 1,500 study and research allowance
Medical insurance, visa/entry fee where required, and participation in at least one extracurricular event
application_method: Review the call and select a programme and university from the published list of 60 eligible Master's programmes at participating universities in Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda and Tanzania
Apply for admission to that university, indicating the intention to apply for the EAC Scholarship Programme and paying the university application fee where applicable
Complete the online EAC Scholarship Application form at https://ee-eu.kobotoolbox.org/J4W9xHf7
Compile the required supporting documents, naming each file with its prescribed document code, and compress them into a single zipped PDF folder

Email the zipped folder to eacsp@iucea.org and scholarships@adroitconsultinternational.com using the subject line format '[Applicant Name] - Application for [Master's Programme] at [University] - Phase II EACSP'
official.application_route: Two-stage regional application: first seek admission to an eligible Master's programme at a partner university in another EAC Partner State, then complete the online EAC scholarship form and email the zipped PDF document set to the programme's two official addresses.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of the eight EAC Partner States - Burundi, Democratic Republic of Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania and Uganda; study must be undertaken in a Partner State other than the applicant's country of citizenship.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - nationals of all eight EAC Partner States may apply, and the award specifically funds study in an EAC Partner State other than the applicant's own (intra-regional mobility).
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Master's programmes in Mathematics, Engineering, Informatics, Science, Technology and Business Science, restricted to the 60 eligible programmes published in the call at participating universities.
official.description: The EAC Scholarship Programme (EACSP) is a regional initiative of the East African Community and the Federal Republic of Germany, implemented by the Inter-University Council for East Africa, that supports academically talented but financially disadvantaged students to pursue Master's studies in an EAC Partner State other than their country of citizenship. Launched in 2018, Phase II commenced in October 2025 and is expected to support at least 280 students across three cohorts, with the vision 'Leadership to Foster Regional Integration.'
official.program_type: Regional Master's scholarship programme (EAC and Federal Republic of Germany initiative, KfW-funded, implemented by IUCEA)
official.english_requirement: Applications must be submitted in English. Supporting documents in languages other than English must be submitted as originals plus copies translated into English by an accredited language translation provider. An English language proficiency certificate such as IELTS or TOEFL is requested as document E24 only 'where applicable'; no minimum score is published.

not_confirmed: Study mode (not stated on the call page)
Minimum English proficiency score (E24 certificate requested only where applicable)
Application window for the next cohort (no future dates published as of 2026-10-10)
verification.notes: Award amounts, scholarship package, eligibility, deadlines, eligible programme list and document checklist were read directly from the IUCEA Cohort 4 call page on iucea.org; the Call for applications index was checked for any newer EACSP cohort call and none was published.

applicant_utility.summary: This KfW-funded IUCEA award pays full tuition, a EUR 380 monthly stipend, return airfare, medical insurance and visa costs for a two-year Master's in Mathematics, Engineering, Informatics, Science, Technology or Business Science at a university in a neighbouring EAC country. Cohort 4 closed on 10 September 2026, so the practical route is the next cohort on the same annual cycle, and the university admission application has to be started first because the scholarship application cannot proceed without it. With only about 120 awards per cohort across the whole region, the financial-needs assessment - bank statements and hardship evidence - carries as much weight as the degree class.
applicant_utility.best_fit: EAC nationals under 35 holding a Second Class Upper Division or Distinction Bachelor's degree who need funding to study outside their home country in a science, technology, engineering, mathematics or business-related field.
application_readiness_checklist: Start the host-university admission application early and keep the admission letter, acknowledgement email, receipt or portal screenshot as E03 proof
Request certified true copies of the Bachelor's degree certificate and transcript, plus accredited English translations if the originals are not in English
If the degree was earned outside the intended host country, begin equating it with the host country's higher-education council before admission
Gather six months of bank statements and any financial-hardship evidence such as fee balance statements or university hardship correspondence so the needs case is consistent
Confirm an academic and a professional referee who will each supply a signed reference letter
Prepare the CV, the colour passport photograph and every file named in the E01-E24 code format before zipping the folder
common_rejection_risks: Applying only to the university and never completing the separate online scholarship form - the two applications are independent
Missing even one mandatory E01-E08 document, which makes the application incomplete and ineligible
Sending one email covering several programmes instead of a separate form and document set per programme
Uncertified transcripts or missing accredited English translations
Submitting after the 17:00 East Africa Time cut-off on the closing date
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: University application fees where applicable, certified-copy and accredited-translation charges, passport or national ID costs, personal spending beyond the EUR 380 stipend, and any costs for dependants, which the package does not cover.
document_audit: Every file must be named '[Document Code] [Document Name]' (e.g. 'E01 National ID') and all files compressed into a single zipped PDF folder
E04 must be certified true copies, and non-English documents need both originals and accredited translations
Degrees obtained outside the host country must be equated by the host country's council before admission, which takes time - start early
The financial-need documents (E06, E09, E22, E23) must tell one consistent story with the CV and payslips, since IUCEA verifies submitted information
alerts: Submitting a university admission application does not constitute a scholarship application - both stages are mandatory
The award cannot be deferred or transferred; failure to take it up at the time of award results in termination
Only shortlisted applicants are contacted, so silence is normal - check spam folders around the December communication date
The next cohort window has historically opened in late August for about three weeks, so monitor the IUCEA 'Call for applications' page from August onwards
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for university admission first, then complete the online EAC scholarship form, then email one zipped PDF document set per programme to eacsp@iucea.org and scholarships@adroitconsultinternational.com with the prescribed subject line.
